{{Short description|Digital marketing technique}}
{{protection padlock|small=yes}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}}
'''Generative engine optimization''' ('''GEO'''), also known as '''answer engine optimization''' (AEO)<ref name="newman2026">{{cite web |last=Newman |first=Nic |date=12 January 2026 |title=Journalism, media, and technology trends and predictions 2026 |url=https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/journalism-media-and-technology-trends-and-predictions-2026 |access-date=30 January 2026 |website=Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism |publisher=University of Oxford |archive-date=30 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130061627/https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/journalism-media-and-technology-trends-and-predictions-2026 |url-status=live }}</ref> and '''artificial intelligence optimization''' (AIO),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fan |first1=Zhenan |last2=Ghaddar |first2=Bissan |last3=Wang |first3=Xinglu |last4=Xing |first4=Linzi |last5=Zhang |first5=Yong |last6=Zhou |first6=Zirui |date=1 July 2026 |title=Artificial intelligence for optimization: Unleashing the potential of parameter generation, model formulation, and solution methods |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0377221725006666 |journal=[[European Journal of Operational Research]] |volume=332 |issue=1 |pages=1–30 |doi=10.1016/j.ejor.2025.08.029 |issn=0377-2217 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> is the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by [[generative artificial intelligence]] (AI) systems. The practice influences the way [[large language model]]s (LLMs) retrieve, summarize, and present information in response to user queries.<ref name="newman2026" /> 

This concept first appeared in response to generative AI technologies being integrated into mainstream search and information retrieval systems.<ref name="herrman2025">{{cite web |last=Herrman |first=John |date=4 August 2025 |title=SEO Is Dead. Say Hello to GEO. |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/seo-is-dead-say-hello-to-geo.html |access-date=11 November 2025 |website=Intelligencer |archive-date=17 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251117001649/https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/seo-is-dead-say-hello-to-geo.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Terminology ==
The term "generative engine optimization" was introduced in a 2023 paper by Pranjal Aggarwal and co-authors, later presented at the [[Special Interest Group on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining|KDD 2024 conference]].<ref name="aggarwal2024">{{cite conference |last1=Aggarwal |first1=Pranjal |last2=Murahari |first2=Vishvak |last3=Rajpurohit |first3=Tanmay |last4=Kalyan |first4=Ashwin |last5=Narasimhan |first5=Karthik |last6=Deshpande |first6=Ameet |date=2024 |title=GEO: Generative Engine Optimization |conference=KDD '24: Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining |arxiv=2311.09735}}</ref> Several overlapping terms describe related practices, and usage varies across practitioners, vendors, and publications, with no consensus definition.<ref name="newman2026" /> Other terms for the same concept include answer engine optimization (AEO), large language model optimization (LLMO), artificial intelligence optimization (AIO), and AI SEO.<ref name="newman2026" />

In 2026, Google published a guide to optimizing for its generative AI search features, which describes "AEO" and "GEO" as terms "you may see used" but argues that "optimizing for generative AI search is optimizing for the search experience, and thus still SEO."<ref name="google-ai-guide">{{cite web |title=Google's Guide to Optimizing for Generative AI Features on Google Search |url=https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide |website=Google Search Central |publisher=[[Google]] |date=10 July 2026 |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> This position had previously been shared at conferences, with 2026 being the first time Google released official documentation stating it.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Southern |first1=Matt G. |date=15 May 2026 |title=Google's New AI Search Guide Calls AEO And GEO 'Still SEO' |url=https://www.searchenginejournal.com/googles-new-ai-search-guide-calls-aeo-and-geo-still-seo/575026/ |website=Search Engine Journal |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Microsoft Bing]] refers to the practice as "generative engine optimization" in its documentation, but does clarify that [[search engine optimization|SEO]] fundamentals "support eligibility for AI-generated experiences."<ref>{{cite web |title=Bing Webmaster Guidelines |url=https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/webmaster-guidelines-30fba23a |website=Bing}}</ref><ref name="sej-bing-geo">{{cite news |last=Southern |first=Matt G. |date=27 February 2026 |title=Bing Adds GEO To Official Guidelines, Expands AI Abuse Definitions |url=https://www.searchenginejournal.com/bing-adds-geo-to-official-guidelines-expands-ai-abuse-definitions/568442/ |work=Search Engine Journal |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> [[Microsoft Advertising]] uses both terms, defining AEO as optimizing for AI agents and assistants such as [[Microsoft Copilot|Copilot]] and GEO as optimizing for generative AI search environments.<ref name="ser-msads-2026">{{cite news |last=Schwartz |first=Barry |date=14 January 2026 |title=Microsoft Advertising Releases Guide To AEO & GEO |url=https://www.seroundtable.com/microsoft-advertiser-guide-to-aeo-geo-40748.html |work=Search Engine Roundtable |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> A [[Perplexity AI|Perplexity]] representative used "GEO" while cautioning against vendors overstating their expertise in it.<ref name="ser-georush-2025">{{cite news |last=Schwartz |first=Barry |date=19 November 2025 |title=Quotes From Google, Microsoft, and Perplexity On GEO Rush |url=https://www.seroundtable.com/google-microsoft-perplexity-geo-rush-40457.html |work=Search Engine Roundtable |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref>

Tools and vendors are similarly divided. [[HubSpot]] uses the term AEO.<ref name="techtarget-hubspot-2026">{{cite news |last=Fluckinger |first=Don |date=14 April 2026 |title=HubSpot builds answer engine optimization into its platform |url=https://www.techtarget.com/searchcustomerexperience/news/366641773/HubSpot-builds-answer-engine-optimization-into-its-platform |work=[[TechTarget]] |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> Profound describes AEO and GEO as the same practice but argues that "GEO" can be confused with geography.<ref name="profound-aeo-geo">{{cite web |last=Lafferty |first=Nick |date=29 June 2025 |title=AEO vs. GEO: Why they're the same thing (and why we prefer AEO) |url=https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/aeo-vs-geo |publisher=Profound |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> [[Adobe Inc.|Adobe]]'s 2025 LLM Optimizer launch was covered as "AI search optimization,"<ref name="techtarget-adobe-2025">{{cite news |last=Fluckinger |first=Don |date=17 June 2025 |title=Adobe takes on AI search optimization with LLM Optimizer |url=https://www.techtarget.com/searchcustomerexperience/news/366626187/Adobe-takes-on-AI-search-optimization-with-LLM-Optimizer |work=[[TechTarget]] |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> while its 2026 Adobe Brand Visibility product was marketed as a GEO platform;<ref name="martech-adobe-2026">{{cite news |last=Pastore |first=Mike |date=17 June 2026 |title=Adobe brings GEO to CX Enterprise with Adobe Brand Visibility |url=https://martech.org/adobe-brings-geo-to-cx-enterprise-with-adobe-brand-visibility/ |work=MarTech |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> the Adobe platform [[Semrush]] markets its tools under "AI SEO" and "AI Visibility."<ref name="semrush-ai-seo">{{cite web |title=Semrush AI Visibility |url=https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/overview/ |publisher=[[Semrush]] |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> [[Sitecore]] referred to the discipline as "answer engine optimization" and "AEO" in
its press release announcing its acquisition of Scrunch.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Sitecore acquires Scrunch to help brands influence discovery and buying decisions in the AI-search era |url=https://www.sitecore.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/2026/06/sitecore-acquires-scrunch-to-help-brands-influence-discovery--and-buying-decisions |publisher=Sitecore |location=New York |date=June 3, 2026 |access-date=September 30, 2026}}</ref> Peec AI describes itself as an "AI search analytics" tool.<ref name="sel-peec-2026">{{cite news |last=Goodwin |first=Danny |date=31 March 2026 |title=AI search engines cite Reddit, YouTube, and LinkedIn most: Study |url=https://searchengineland.com/ai-search-engines-cite-reddit-youtube-and-linkedin-most-study-473138 |work=Search Engine Land |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref>

Writing for [[Forrester Research]], Nikhil Lai argued in 2025 that answer engine optimization (and related terms) are "significantly, but not fundamentally, different from SEO" and that advocates of terms like AEO, GEO, AIO, and LLMO "tend to exaggerate SEO and AEO's differences to carve a startup-sized hole in marketers' tech stacks."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lai |first1=Nikhil |title=SEO's Hype-Fueled Move To The Center Of The Marketing Mix |url=https://www.forrester.com/blogs/seos-hype-fueled-move-to-the-center-of-the-marketing-mix/ |website=Forrester}}</ref> Venture capital firm [[Andreessen Horowitz]] used "GEO" in a 2025 essay on the field.<ref name="a16z-geo-2025">{{cite web |last1=Cohen |first1=Zach |last2=Amble |first2=Seema |date=May 2025 |title=How Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Rewrites the Rules of Search |url=https://a16z.com/geo-over-seo/ |publisher=[[Andreessen Horowitz]] |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref>

== Tools ==
Various tools are used to monitor how websites and brands are cited, referenced, or incorporated into responses produced by [[large language models]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brands target AI chatbots as users switch from Google search |url=https://www.ft.com/content/9cc6cc0b-759f-4b8e-9ed1-9e32ad0fe22f?utm |website=Financial Times |access-date=26 February 2026 |archive-date=5 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260505061444/https://www.ft.com/content/9cc6cc0b-759f-4b8e-9ed1-9e32ad0fe22f?utm |url-status=live }}</ref> This includes free tools like the AI Performance report in [[Bing Webmaster Tools]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Danny |title=Bing Webmaster Tools officially adds AI Performance report |url=https://searchengineland.com/bing-webmaster-tools-ai-performance-report-468751 |website=Search Engine Land}}</ref> and Search Generative AI performance reports in [[Google Search Console]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schwartz |first1=Barry |title=Google Search Console AI performance reports and controls to block your content in AI responses |url=https://searchengineland.com/google-search-console-ai-performance-reports-and-controls-to-block-your-content-in-ai-responses-479298 |website=Search Engine Land}}</ref>

While the efficacy of third-party tools is debated within the overall GEO and SEO industries,<ref name="Digiday-McCoy-2026">{{cite news |last=McCoy |first=Kimeko |date=2026-05-01 |title=Marketers question expensive AI visibility tools as inconsistent results fuel skepticism |url=https://digiday.com/marketing/marketers-question-expensive-ai-visibility-tools-as-inconsistent-results-fuel-skepticism/ |work=[[Digiday]] |access-date=2026-09-30}}</ref><ref name="SEJ-Montti-2026">{{cite news |last=Montti |first=Roger |date=2026-06-07 |title=Google's New Guidance Claims Authority Over SEO, Tools, And AEO/GEO |url=https://www.searchenginejournal.com/googles-new-guidance-claims-authority-over-seo-tools-and-aeo-geo/578162/ |work=Search Engine Journal |access-date=2026-09-30}}</ref> some of the largest tools used to track and improve generative engine optimization include legacy SEO tools like Ahrefs<ref name="Digiday-McCoy-2026"/> and [[Semrush]],<ref name="Digiday-McCoy-2026"/><ref name="TechTarget-Semrush-2025">{{cite news |last=Fluckinger |first=Don |date=2025-11-20 |title=Adobe bolsters AI SEO with planned $1.9B Semrush acquisition |url=https://www.techtarget.com/enterprise-software/news/366634642/Adobe-bolsters-AI-SEO-with-planned-19B-Semrush-acquisition |work=[[TechTarget]] |access-date=2026-09-30}}</ref> along with startups Profound<ref name="Digiday-McCoy-2026"/><ref name="Fortune-Profound-2026">{{cite news |last=Lazarus |first=Lily Mae |date=2026-02-24 |title=Exclusive: As AI threatens search, Profound raises $96 million to help brands stay visible |url=https://fortune.com/2026/02/24/exclusive-as-ai-threatens-search-profound-raises-96-million-to-help-brands-stay-visible/ |work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |access-date=2026-09-30}}</ref> and [[Scrunch]].<ref name="FastCo-Beer-2026">{{cite news |last=Beer |first=Jeff |date=2026-04-09 |title=Brands vs. bots: CMOs, ad agencies tell all about what they've learned marketing to our new AI overlords |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91522570/brands-vs-bots-cmos-ad-agencies-tell-all-about-what-theyve-learned-marketing-to-our-new-ai-overlords |work=[[Fast Company]] |access-date=2026-09-30}}</ref><ref name="Bloomberg-Scrunch-2026">{{cite news |title=Sitecore Said to Acquire Scrunch for $225 Million |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-03/sitecore-said-to-acquire-scrunch-for-225-million |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=2026-06-03 |access-date=2026-09-30 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
